variable_coverage.construction: Deflate annual Compustat Global/NA XOPR using the country-year GDP deflator and compute ln(XOPR_t)−ln(XOPR_{t−1}); use the paper’s main XOPR measure excluding depreciation. Local xopr is a candidate field and its exact depreciation treatment is not confirmed.
Deflate annual SALE by the same country-specific GDP deflator and compute ln(SALE_t)−ln(SALE_{t−1}). Preserve the fiscal-year label and date separately.

Multiply the mean-zero EPL index, defined as (late-1990s REGEPL+TEMPEPL)/2, by current deflated DlnSALE. The public OECD components are available; firm-country linking and sample means require reconstruction.
Multiply contemporaneous annual real GDPGROWTH_{n,t} by DlnSALE_t. Current WDI provides a public candidate series; exact source vintage, country key and firm-year alignment remain unverified.
Compute AINT_t=ln(AT_t/SALE_t) and multiply it by current deflated DlnSALE. AINT and continuous controls are mean-zero rescaled per footnote 39.
Multiply the paper-defined common-law indicator (Australia, Canada, Ireland, UK, US = 1; other sample countries = 0) by current deflated DlnSALE.

Code DEC_t=1 when sales decrease in year t and multiply DEC_t by current deflated DlnSALE. The paper does not separately state whether the decrease flag is computed on nominal or deflated sales; use of the real SALE definition is a candidate mapping.
Multiply the mean-zero country EPL index, DEC_t and current deflated DlnSALE. EPL is static at the late-1990s reference; DEC_t is contemporaneous.

Multiply DEC_{t−1}, DEC_t and current deflated DlnSALE. DEC_{t−1} is a prior-year sales-decrease indicator and requires sales at t−1 and t−2; do not absorb that t−2 raw input into the start of the estimation sample.
Multiply contemporaneous GDPGROWTH_{n,t}, DEC_t and current deflated DlnSALE; the country-year growth input is contemporaneous even though the sales difference needs t−1.
Multiply current AINT_t, DEC_t and current deflated DlnSALE; AINT is ln(AT_t/SALE_t), with the continuous control mean-zero rescaled.
Multiply the paper-defined common-law-country indicator, DEC_t and current deflated DlnSALE.

design_coverage.reason: Sample screen and count are reported, but the exact firm-year roster, country/industry/currency mapping, 19-country identity bridge and local population coverage remain unresolved.

Global and North America statements are jointly required. The historical firm-country field, native-currency classification, OECD country codes, and WDI/OECD keys are not linked or coverage-confirmed.

The selected Model A equation is pooled across the firm-year panel without country or year fixed effects; those effects appear only in a separate sensitivity specification. Country-level random slope shocks are part of the composite error, not a fitted fixed-effects dimension.
Two-way clustering is by country and year; cluster-key construction must follow the same historical country and annual t mapping as the analysis panel.
No regression weights are reported for Model A.

The authors combine the level-1 and country-level equations and estimate pooled OLS under their stated zero-mean/exogeneity assumptions; do not substitute a random-coefficients ML or separate country-by-country fits.

Deflate XOPR and SALE by country-specific GDP deflators; form first differences, DEC and AINT; apply current/two-prior-year screens, currency and nonfinancial filters, 1% tail exclusion and current/prior-year sales-change screens. Continuous controls and EPL are mean-zero rescaled. Exact source/vintage and screen implementation still need mapping.

implementation_issues.description: The article reports 128,333 firm-years and 15,833 firms but does not give an exact observation roster or Global/North America allocation. Local probes confirm selected columns/readability only; no coordinator confirmation establishes the 1988–2008 source history or 1990–2008 estimation population.

The main XOPR measure excludes depreciation, while the local Compustat label for xopr is only “Operating Expenses - Total.” The exact source calculation and product mapping for both Global and North America remain unverified.

Firm-country selection, native-currency screening and joins to World Bank/OECD country keys are not fully specified. Available fic/loc fields are current identifiers, not verified historical country assignments; the non-financial industry screen also has no reported code rule.

The article cites the World Bank Databank but gives no exact GDP-deflator indicator code or vintage. Current WDI provides a GDP deflator index and annual inflation series; the exact deflator field used for real XOPR/SALE is not confirmed, and current values may differ from the paper-era snapshot.

The paper cites World Bank annual GDP growth without an indicator code or frozen vintage; current NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG is a public candidate, but the historical values, full 19-country-year coverage and the Compustat fyear-to-calendar-year join are not verified.

The paper specifies 1% tail exclusions and sales-change screens but does not state the percentile reference population/order of operations. Reproduce the stated filters without substituting winsorization; exact sample recovery remains unverified.

DEC is defined as a sales decrease, and the equation includes prior-year DEC(t−1), but the separate construction of the decrease flag from nominal versus deflated sales is not stated. Preserve the explicit t−1 indicator and its t−2 raw sales need.

review_notes: Only the frozen Model A main sample, Table 5 column (a), is assessed. Columns (b)–(d), Table 6–7 specifications and other robustness analyses are excluded.

The article’s source window is Compustat 1988–2008, but the retained estimation panel is 1990–2008 because the first two years support differences, prior-decrease predictors and screening. The DEC(t−1) construction separately requires SALES through t−2.
Compustat Global and North America are jointly required components; their local routes are not substitutes for one another and no local coverage confirmation establishes the sample.
The official OECD table is the cited late-1990s EPL source; WDI current series are public candidates but not evidence of the paper’s historical World Bank vintage or complete sample-country coverage.
Equation (3) and its printed PDF rendering were inspected: Model A includes DEC(t−1) in the current sales-decrease slope and is estimated by pooled OLS with two-way country/year clustering.
